AllOf.description:
Conjunction: holds when every child predicate holds.

Attributes:
    kind: Discriminator, always ``"all"``.
    predicates: Children, evaluated left to right with short-circuit.
AllOf.title: AllOf

AnyOf.description:
Disjunction: holds when at least one child predicate holds.

Attributes:
    kind: Discriminator, always ``"any"``.
    predicates: Children, evaluated left to right with short-circuit.
AnyOf.title: AnyOf

AttributionSummary.description:
Flexible attribution evidence from a domain reasoner.

Accommodates three forms of model attribution — all optional — to support
the range of what different model types can produce:

- ``feature_contributions``: per-event contributions from any attribution
  method (why THIS prediction for THIS event).
- ``feature_importance``: global model-level weights from training
  (which features matter most in general — not per-event).
- ``narrative``: free-form explanation for cases where neither structured
  form applies (e.g., vendor black-box models, rule-based reasoners).

At least one field should be populated for meaningful audit quality.
The framework stores this verbatim in the DecisionBundle without
interpreting its contents.

Attributes:
    feature_contributions: Per-event feature contributions ranked by
        magnitude. Present when the model produces per-observation
        attribution (SHAP, LIME, rule weights, etc.). None when
        attribution is not available.
    feature_importance: Global feature weight map from model training
        (feature name → importance score). Provides model-level
        explainability when per-event attribution is unavailable.
    narrative: Free-form explanation. Used when neither structured form
        applies, or to supplement them with domain context.
AttributionSummary.title: AttributionSummary

BypassCheck.description:
The ledger's evaluation of one registered bypass rule for a record.

Stored in the bundle with the rule itself — for the cited rule and for
every other rule the reasoner registers — so replay re-evaluates the
exact predicates that were checked, without the registration.

Attributes:
    rule: The registered rule, as evaluated.
    observed: The submission's value for every field the predicate
        references (fields the evidence lacks are omitted).
    holds: Whether the predicate held against the evidence. ``False``
        when it could not be evaluated.
    error: Why the predicate could not be evaluated (a missing feature,
        a non-numeric operand), or ``None``.
BypassCheck.title: BypassCheck

BypassCitation.description:
The registered bypass rule a recorded decision cites.

Attributes:
    rule_id: A ``BypassRule.rule_id`` from the reasoner's registration.
    rule_version: Optional pin. When set it must equal the registered
        rule's ``version``, so a reasoner built against an older rule
        cannot record under a newer one unnoticed.
BypassCitation.title: BypassCitation

BypassRule.description:
A registered condition under which a reasoner may record a decision.

A recorded submission cites a rule by ``rule_id``. The ledger accepts
the citation only when the rule is registered and the submission's
``proposed_action`` is the rule's ``action``; it then evaluates
``predicate`` against the submission's ``reasoner_context`` (the
``label_value`` and ``feature_set`` the reasoner reported), records
whether it holds, and snapshots the rule into the bundle so replay can
evaluate it again from the bundle alone. The predicate language is the
one the rules gate uses (``core.gate.predicate``): pure, closed, and
JSON-serializable.

Attributes:
    rule_id: Identifier a recorded submission cites; unique within the
        registration.
    version: Version label recorded with every decision that cites the
        rule. Change it whenever the predicate or action changes.
    description: Human-readable intent of the rule.
    predicate: When the rule applies, over ``label_value`` and
        ``feature_set.<name>``.
    action: The one action the rule justifies recording. A reasoner
        that may record different actions under different conditions
        registers one rule per action.
BypassRule.title: BypassRule

Compare.description:
Leaf node: compare one field of the subject with a constant.

Attributes:
    kind: Discriminator, always ``"compare"``.
    field: ``"label_value"`` or ``"feature_set.<name>"``.
    op: One of ``eq``, ``ne``, ``lt``, ``le``, ``gt``, ``ge``, ``in``,
        ``not_in``.
    value: The constant. A number for ordering operators, a non-empty
        list of scalars for ``in`` / ``not_in``, any scalar otherwise.
Compare.title: Compare

Contribution.description:
Per-event feature contribution from a domain reasoner.

Carried in ``AttributionSummary.feature_contributions`` to provide
per-observation feature attribution in the DecisionBundle.

Works with any feature attribution method: SHAP values, LIME
coefficients, rule weights, attention scores, etc. Sign and magnitude
semantics are defined by ``method`` — the framework carries the value
without interpreting it. For example, SHAP values are signed (positive
pushes the prediction toward the positive class; negative pushes away),
while attention scores are typically non-negative.

Attributes:
    feature_name: Name of the contributing feature (snake_case).
    feature_value: Raw feature value as seen by the model at inference
        time.
    method: Attribution method that produced the contribution value
        (e.g., ``"shap"``, ``"lime"``, ``"rule_weight"``,
        ``"attention"``). Set by the domain assembler.
        Descriptive — the framework never switches on this field.
    value: Numeric contribution value from the attribution method.
        Sign and magnitude semantics vary by method — see ``method``.
Contribution.title: Contribution

DecisionAction.description:
Final action the enforcement layer produces for a governed decision.

Members are declared in ascending severity: ALLOW, CHALLENGE, HOLD, BLOCK.
Severity ordering is not a property of this enum: the conjunction
combinator (``core.gate.combinator``) owns the authoritative ranking,
``SEVERITY_ORDER``, which enforcement and the combinator both read.

.. warning::
    ``StrEnum`` comparison is lexicographic — ``BLOCK < CHALLENGE``
    alphabetically. Never use ``<`` / ``>`` on ``DecisionAction`` to
    determine severity.

Attributes:
    ALLOW: No friction. The request proceeds without additional controls.
    CHALLENGE: A friction control is applied before the request proceeds.
        The specific control is domain-defined (e.g., step-up
        authentication, CAPTCHA, manual approval gate).
    HOLD: The request is suspended pending asynchronous human review.
        No automated resolution occurs until the review is completed.
    BLOCK: The request is immediately rejected. No further pipeline
        processing occurs.
DecisionAction.title: DecisionAction

EnforcementDecision.description:
Decision-time action plus override log from the deterministic enforcement layer.

The enforcement layer is purely rule-based — no calls to the gate,
the domain reasoner, or any other non-deterministic component. Every
execution path is deterministic given the same inputs. This is what
makes replay work: re-executing enforcement against the cached gate
outputs in a bundle must produce the same ``decision_action``.

For non-terminal actions (CHALLENGE, HOLD), the ultimately-realized
action is recorded later in the resolution attempt log (see
``core.resolution``). The enforcement layer's job ends at producing
this decision; resolution is a separate, append-only artifact.

Attributes:
    decision_action: The action this decision produces. Immutable.
        For terminal actions (ALLOW, BLOCK) this is the realized
        action; for non-terminal actions (CHALLENGE, HOLD) the
        realized action is computed from the resolution attempt log.
    enforcement_rule_applied: The rule that fired, if any: a gate-level
        tier for a gate's enforcement, a decision-level rule for the
        decision's. ``None`` when no rule overrode the result.
    override_log: Ordered list of rule evaluations and outcomes.
        Records every trigger check performed, including those that
        did not fire.
EnforcementDecision.title: EnforcementDecision

EntityDerivation.description:
How a subject's id follows from an enterprise key.

Attributes:
    namespace_uuid: The UUID5 namespace.
    enterprise_key: The key under it.
EntityDerivation.title: EntityDerivation

EvidenceRef.description:
A reference to one source a gate relied on (generalizes a citation).

Attributes:
    source_id: Stable identifier of the source (a document id, the id
        and version of a set of rules, a lookup table name).
    locator: Optional position inside the source (a section path, a
        rule id, a row key). ``None`` when the source is atomic.
    jurisdictions: Regulatory jurisdiction tags the source carries.
        Empty for sources that have no jurisdiction. Enforcement's
        jurisdiction-conflict tier reads the union across a gate's
        evidence and checks it against the reasoner's conflict groups.
    content_hash: The SHA-256 digest (lowercase hex) of the exact
        content the gate relied on from this source, as the gate saw it
        (an excerpt, a whole set of rules). Anyone holding that content
        can recompute and compare it; the framework stores it and never
        reads the content. ``None`` when the gate records no digest
        (DR-34).
    artifact_hash: The SHA-256 digest (lowercase hex) of the artifact
        the ledger's evidence escrow holds for this reference: the
        source's content as the gate read it while deciding, which the
        gate handed to the escrow (``decisionledger.evidence_artifacts``,
        DR-34). The gate sets it only from what the escrow returned, so
        it is ``None`` when the gate escrows nothing for the reference
        or the deployment runs with escrow off.
EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

GateContext.description:
Gate dispatch envelope — selects the gate and carries its configuration.

Built by the reasoner from its own event, feature, and scoring
artifacts. The framework uses ``gate_id`` for dispatch and authorization,
then passes ``gate_config`` through to the selected gate implementation.

Attributes:
    gate_id: Identifier of the gate this envelope addresses (e.g.,
        ``"policy"``). Must name a gate in the reasoner's gate set.
    gate_config: Gate-specific configuration, as JSON values (it is
        stored verbatim in the bundle and must survive the round trip).
        Validated against the gate's declared ``config_model`` at intake
        when it has one; otherwise interpreted only by the gate.
        ``None`` means no gate-specific config.
GateContext.title: GateContext

GateInput.description:
The framework's record of one gate invocation.

Attributes:
    gate_id: Identifier of the gate the framework dispatched to. Mirrors
        the ``GateContext.gate_id`` it dispatched on.
GateInput.title: GateInput

GateOutput.description:
Universal output contract for a gate invocation (open per DR-28).

Attributes:
    gate_id: Identifier of the gate that ran. Equals the
        ``GateContext.gate_id`` the framework dispatched on.
    deterministic: ``True`` when the gate is a pure function of its
        input (the plugin's declared value, recorded here so replay
        applies the same tiers). Deterministic gates skip enforcement
        Tiers 2 (adversarial probe) and 4 (low confidence).
    verdict: The validated verdict enforcement consumes. ``None`` when
        the gate produced no valid verdict; enforcement routes to HOLD
        via the schema-failure tier and ``extra`` may carry forensics.
        When present, ``verdict.gate_id`` equals ``gate_id``.
    evidence: References to the sources the gate relied on. Enforcement
        Tier 5 (jurisdiction conflict) runs only when at least one
        reference carries jurisdictions.
    evidence_snapshot: Opaque, gate-owned JSON describing what the gate
        consulted, stored verbatim for audit and replay. ``None`` when
        the gate has nothing to record.
    extra: Opaque, gate-specific output fields (JSON values). The
        framework stores them without interpretation.
GateOutput.title: GateOutput

GateRecord.description:
What happened at one gate of a decision's gate set.

Field semantics by ``status``:

* ``ran`` — the framework invoked the gate (``input``) and it returned a
  valid universal output (``output``); ``enforcement`` holds the
  gate-level tiers applied to it.
* ``failed`` — the gate produced no usable output: it raised, timed out,
  returned something other than a plain ``GateOutput`` for itself, or no
  gate is composed under its id. ``output`` is ``None``, ``reason`` says
  why, ``input`` is set when the framework did invoke it, and
  ``enforcement`` holds the fail-closed result (the schema-failure tier:
  HOLD).
* ``skipped`` — the framework did not invoke the gate: an advisory gate
  on a recorded decision, or any advisory gate once the decision was
  already BLOCK. ``reason`` says which; nothing else is set.

Attributes:
    gate_id: The gate.
    mandatory: Whether the gate was mandatory for this decision (bound
        mandatory by the registration or mandated by the deployment).
    status: ``ran`` | ``skipped`` | ``failed``.
    reason: Why the gate was skipped or failed; ``None`` when it ran.
    input: The framework's record that it invoked the gate.
    output: The gate's universal output (opaque extension included).
    enforcement: Gate-level enforcement of this gate's output.
    duration_ms: Wall-clock time of the gate call, or ``None`` when the
        gate was not invoked.
GateRecord.title: GateRecord

GateVerdict.description:
Universal, enforcement-consumable verdict.

Carries only the fields ``app.enforcement.resolver`` reads.
Explanation artifacts the framework does not interpret live in the
gate's ``GateOutput`` extension, not here.

Attributes:
    gate_id: Identifier of the gate that produced this verdict. Equals
        the enclosing ``GateOutput.gate_id``.
    permitted_actions: Actions the gate permits for this event.
        Enforcement selects the most conservative action from this list.
    required_controls: Controls that must be applied alongside the
        action (e.g., ``"log_step_up_reason"``,
        ``"adversarial_probe_detected"``,
        ``"jurisdiction_conflict"``). Enforcement matches against
        sentinel values.
    confidence: Gate's self-reported confidence in the verdict, in
        [0.0, 1.0]. Low confidence + high-risk action triggers a HOLD
        override in enforcement.
    escalate_to_human: True if the gate recommends human review
        regardless of the chosen action.
    escalation_reason: Required when ``escalate_to_human`` is True;
        describes the specific concern requiring human judgment.
GateVerdict.title: GateVerdict

IdentityProvenance.description:
How a decision's subject was established.

Attributes:
    native_namespace: The namespace of the native subject the reasoner
        named; ``None`` when its submission named none.
    native_subject_id: That native subject's key; ``None`` likewise.
    resolved_by: Who established the subject: the active resolver's id,
        or ``passthrough`` when the ledger kept the reasoner's own.
    crosswalk_version: The version of the mapping the resolver used, if
        it versions one.
    method: ``deterministic``, ``probabilistic``, or ``unresolved``.
    confidence: The match confidence, in [0, 1]: set exactly when the
        method is ``probabilistic``.
    resolved_at: When the subject was established (timezone-aware).
    reason: Why the subject is unresolved (no resolver is active, the
        resolver found no match, failed, or timed out, ...): set exactly
        when the method is ``unresolved``.
IdentityProvenance.title: IdentityProvenance

LabelType.description:
Classification of the domain model's output type.

Attributes:
    NUMERICAL: Continuous score output (e.g., probability ∈ [0.0, 1.0]).
        Typical of regression models and probability estimators.
    CATEGORICAL: Discrete class label output (e.g., ``"POSITIVE"``,
        ``"NEGATIVE"``). Typical of classifiers with a hard decision
        boundary.
LabelType.title: LabelType

NativeSubject.description:
The subject as the reasoner knows it: a key in one of its namespaces.

Carried on a ``Submission`` (``native_subject``). The ledger resolves it
to the decision's subject through the active identity resolver; when the
namespace is one the reasoner's registration declares, the reasoner's
own ``entity_id`` must be the one the declaration derives
(``NATIVE_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`` otherwise).

Attributes:
    native_namespace: The namespace the key belongs to, in the
        reasoner's terms (the system it comes from, for example).
    native_subject_id: The subject's key in that namespace.
NativeSubject.title: NativeSubject

Not.description:
Negation: holds when its child predicate does not.

Attributes:
    kind: Discriminator, always ``"not"``.
    predicate: The negated child.
Not.title: Not

ReasonerContext.description:
Generic lattice for domain reasoner evidence submitted to DecisionLedger.

All fields are domain-agnostic. Domain assemblers translate their internal
model output types into this contract before submitting to the
framework. The framework stores ReasonerContext verbatim in the
DecisionBundle (inside the stored submission).

``label_type``, ``label_name``, and ``label_value`` together describe the
model's prediction in a self-documenting way that is interpretable without
domain knowledge — for example, a bundle reader can understand
``label_type=NUMERICAL, label_name="risk_score", label_value=0.87``
without knowing anything about the originating domain.

``feature_set`` captures the complete feature snapshot at the time of
prediction. This is what makes decisions replayable and auditable from
the DecisionBundle without calling back to the source reasoner.

An LLM-agent reasoner (one that decides with a model call and tools —
for example an agent submitting through the MCP tools — rather than a
trained scorer) fills the same fields with what it actually ran. The
ledger stores them verbatim and auditors read them, so an optional field
the agent cannot fill truthfully stays empty; it is never a placeholder:

- ``model_version``: the provider's model id exactly as called (for
  example ``"claude-opus-5-5"``), not an invented version label.
- ``model_artifact_sha256``: the SHA-256 of the exact prompt the agent
  ran (system and instruction text, rendered), so two decisions with
  the same digest ran the same instructions; ``None`` when no prompt is
  under the reasoner's control.
- ``inference_latency_ms``: wall-clock time of the agent's run up to its
  proposal.
- ``label_type`` / ``label_name`` / ``label_value``: the agent's own
  output that its bypass rules read — a ``CATEGORICAL`` verdict such as
  ``label_name="recommended_action"``, or a ``NUMERICAL`` score such as
  ``label_name="risk_score"`` — not a restatement of the proposal.
- ``feature_set``: the scalar inputs the agent actually consulted (tool
  results it read, flags it computed), plus ``tool_trace_sha256``: the
  SHA-256 of its ordered tool-call trace, as a string.
- ``attribution.narrative``: the agent's stated reasoning, verbatim.

Attributes:
    reasoner_id: Machine identifier for this reasoner, matching the
        DecisionLedger registration record. Used as the stable key for
        cross-bundle queries and comparisons.
    reasoner_name: Human-readable display name. Recorded in the bundle
        for display contexts — dashboards, review packets, audit
        reports.
    model_version: Model artifact version string. Enables detection of
        version drift between the original decision and any
        retrospective replay.
    model_artifact_sha256: SHA-256 hex digest of the model binary at
        load time. Provides content-addressable proof of which exact
        artifact produced the prediction — compare against a candidate
        file to verify. ``None`` for API-based or vendor models where
        no local artifact exists. Artifact storage and discovery are
        the domain's responsibility (or an external model registry's).
    inference_latency_ms: Wall-clock inference time in milliseconds.
        Recorded in the bundle latency breakdown. ``None`` for batch
        reasoners where per-observation latency is not meaningful.
    label_type: Whether the model output is a continuous score or a
        discrete class label.
    label_name: Semantic name of the output label
        (e.g., ``"risk_score"``, ``"fraud_probability"``,
        ``"churn_label"``). Self-documents the prediction in the bundle.
    label_value: The model's prediction. ``float`` for ``NUMERICAL``;
        ``str`` for ``CATEGORICAL``.
    feature_set: Complete snapshot of the named feature values the model
        consumed at prediction time. Enables audit and replay without
        calling back to the source reasoner. Keys are feature names
        (snake_case); values are the raw feature values.
    attribution: Optional attribution evidence. Strongly encouraged for
        audit quality — omitting it reduces the explainability of
        decisions in the bundle.
ReasonerContext.title: ReasonerContext

RelatedEntity.description:
A subject related to the decision's subject, as the resolver reports it.

Flat from the subject and typed: the resolver declares every
``relationship_type`` it emits when it is composed, and the ledger
refuses any other. Cardinality and meaning are the resolver's.

Attributes:
    relationship_type: The relationship, one of the resolver's declared
        types.
    entity_type: The related subject's type.
    entity_id: The related subject's id.
RelatedEntity.title: RelatedEntity

ResolvedIdentity.description:
A decision's subject: the bundle's identity layer.

Attributes:
    entity_id: The subject's id: the bundle's subject, its timeline key.
    entity_type: The subject's type (``"customer"``, ``"account"``, ...).
    derivation: The namespace and enterprise key the id derives from;
        the model recomputes ``entity_id`` from it and refuses a
        mismatch. Required of a resolved subject; ``None`` only for an
        unresolved subject that is the reasoner's asserted ``entity_id``.
    provenance: Who established the subject, how, and when.
    related: The subject's related subjects, each ``(relationship_type,
        entity_id)`` once. An unresolved subject has none.
ResolvedIdentity.title: ResolvedIdentity

Submission.description:
One decision a reasoner hands the ledger, to record or to gate.

Attributes:
    schema_version: Wire schema version; always ``2``.
    reasoner_id: The submitting reasoner. Must equal
        ``reasoner_context.reasoner_id``.
    event_id: Reasoner-assigned unique id of the event the decision is
        about. The default idempotency key and the log correlation id.
    timestamp: When the event occurred (timezone-aware).
    entity_id: The reasoner's own UUID for the subject it scored
        (UUID5 of its native key under its namespace). The decision's
        subject is the identity the ledger resolves
        (``DecisionBundle.identity``, DR-32): the same id when no
        resolver matches the subject, an enterprise subject's when one
        does.
    entity_type: Classification of that subject (``"account"``,
        ``"customer"``, ...).
    native_subject: The subject in the reasoner's own terms (a native
        namespace and key), which the ledger resolves through the
        deployment's identity resolver; ``None`` when the reasoner names
        none (its ``entity_id`` is then recorded as the subject,
        unresolved). In a namespace the reasoner's registration
        declares, ``entity_id`` and ``entity_type`` must be the ones the
        declaration derives.
    mode: ``"record"`` or ``"gate"``.
    proposed_action: The reasoner's action. Required to record (it is
        the decision); optional to gate (a floor: the ledger's result is
        never less restrictive than a proposal).
    bypass: The bypass rule a record cites. Required exactly when
        ``mode == "record"``.
    reasoner_context: The reasoner's evidence: model identity, the
        prediction, and the complete feature snapshot it used.
    gate_contexts: One dispatch envelope per gate, each ``gate_id`` at
        most once.
    raw_event: The reasoner's event as JSON, stored verbatim and never
        interpreted by the ledger.
Submission.title: Submission

description:
Complete, replayable audit record for every decision (schema version 2).

Stored in PostgreSQL (``decisionledger.decision_bundles``), indexed by
``decision_id``. Every field is logged at decision time — nothing is
computed on read, and the row is never updated once written.

Replay guarantee: given a bundle and its reasoner's enforcement profile
(the registration's novel-entity feature and jurisdiction conflict
groups), re-running the gate-level tiers on each stored gate output,
re-evaluating the stored bypass rules against the stored submission's
evidence, and re-running the decision-level rules and the combinator
produce the same ``decision_action``. Replay does **not** re-invoke any
gate, reads no corpus, and needs no reasoner code.

Action vocabulary:
    * ``decision_action`` — the action this bundle produced at decision
      time. Immutable.
    * ``resolution_action`` — for non-terminal decisions (CHALLENGE,
      HOLD), the action a resolver later produced. Lives on
      ``core.resolution.ResolutionAttempt`` rows; never on the bundle.
    * ``realized_action`` — the action ultimately taken on the entity,
      computed from the bundle plus the resolution attempt log; never
      stored.

Attributes:
    schema_version: Always ``2``.
    decision_id: UUID of this decision record.
    created_at: When the bundle was constructed (UTC).
    submission: The reasoner's submission, verbatim — identity, mode,
        proposal and citation, evidence, gate contexts, and its opaque
        ``raw_event``.
    identity: The decision's subject as the ledger resolved it before
        any gate ran (DR-32): the subject's id and type, how the id was
        derived, the provenance of the mapping (resolver, crosswalk
        version, method, confidence, time, and why an unresolved
        subject is unresolved), and the subject's related subjects.
        ``entity_id`` is the bundle's timeline key. ``None`` only on a
        bundle written before the identity contract; such a bundle's
        subject is ``submission.entity_id``.
    idempotency_key: Deduplication key (the event id unless the caller
        supplied one).
    ingestion_timestamp: When the ledger received the submission (over
        HTTP or through a client; the event's own time is
        ``submission.timestamp``).
    gates: One record per gate in the decision's gate set, mandatory
        gates first, each in gate-set order.
    decision_action: The action this decision produced.
    decision_level_rule: The decision-level rule that fired, if any
        (not necessarily the one that set the final action — a mandatory
        gate may still be stricter; the combinator line says what did):
        ``tier3_novel_entity`` (a gated decision about a novel entity,
        its advisory verdicts held for review, unless an advisory gate's
        own Tier 1 or 2 outranked it), ``bypass_rule_not_satisfied`` (a
        record whose cited rule did not hold: HOLD floor), or
        ``bypass_rule_superseded`` (a record citing a rule while another
        registered rule that also holds justifies a stricter action:
        floor at that action).
    override_log: The decision-level trail — the bypass check or the
        novel-entity tier, then the combinator line. Each gate's own
        tier log is in its ``GateRecord.enforcement``.
    bypass_rule_holds: For a record, whether the cited rule held
        against the submission's evidence; ``None`` for a gated
        decision. Equals ``bypass_check.holds``.
    bypass_check: For a record, the cited rule as evaluated (snapshot)
        and the values it read; ``None`` for a gated decision.
    other_bypass_checks: For a record, every other rule the reasoner
        registers, as evaluated (snapshots), so replay can re-check that
        no stricter rule also held; empty for a gated decision.
    registration_version: The version (content address) of the
        reasoner's registration the decision was made under (DR-31).
        Replay enforces against that version's snapshot, served at
        ``GET /api/v1/reasoners/{reasoner_id}/registrations/{version}``.
        ``None`` only on a bundle written before registrations were
        versioned.
    latency_breakdown: The ledger's own steps in milliseconds:
        ``gate_ms`` (wall-clock time of the whole gate phase; each
        gate's own time is in its record) and ``enforcement_ms``, plus
        any step an in-process caller of ``submit`` reported. A reasoner
        reports its own timings itself.
title: DecisionBundle
